abstract:
We examine how a profit-driven platform designs its recommender policies under varying privacy protection regimes. We demonstrate a functional equivalence between opt-out protection and unprotected privacy. Notably, granting consumers the autonomy to misrepresent personal data can compel the platform to distort recommendations, inadvertently harming both parties. When recommendations are purely informative, such privacy controls can deter personalization entirely. However, when recommendations also serve an allocative role—controlling product access—algorithmic discrimination may emerge, restricting the disadvantaged minority from valuable opportunities. These findings remain robust even with endogenous profit margins.
                  This paper was accepted by Omar Besbes, revenue management and market analytics.
                  Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.05007 .

ob.tldr: 分析利润驱动平台在不同隐私保护制度下设计推荐政策。研究发现，选择退出机制与无保护在功能上等价；允许消费者误报数据会扭曲推荐，纯信息型推荐可能失去个性化，兼具产品分配功能时则会产生算法歧视，限制弱势群体的机会。

title: Recommender Systems Under Privacy Protection
